newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to pick adviser for telecoms privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Romania to pick adviser for telecoms privatisation.

text.p: Romania's Communications Ministry said on Friday 10 bank consortia had been short-listed for selection as consultants on the privatisation of monopoly telephone utility Romtelecom RA.
The ministry hopes to be able to strike a contract with a strategic investor in Romtelecom by mid-1998.

"Concrete offers from the 10 banks are expected before May 26 and we intend to conclude a consultancy contract by July," Dan Georgescu, adviser to Romania's Communications Minister, told a four-day Crans Montana Forum in Bucharest.
He said the 10 consortia were selected from a total 36 investment banks which expressed interest in Romania's plans to sell around 30 percent in its telephone operator to a strategic investor.
These banks are backed by legal advisers and auditing firms, Georgescu said.
The 10 consortia include ABN AMRO Bank plus N M Rothschild & Sons Lts, Credit Suisse First Boston (Europe) Ltd, Goldman Sachs, J P Morgan and Lazard Houses.

Also selected were Lehman Brothers plus LCF Rothschild, Merrill Lynch International, Morgan Stanley & Co Ltd, SBC Warburg plus Investmentbank Austria and Union Bank of Switzerland plus Creditanstalt Investment Bank.
"The selected consultant will give financial, legal and technical aid in Romtelecom's privatisation," Georgescu said.
He said selloff of the Romtelecom stake would follow its turning into a shareholding company with the state as the sole stockholder.
Romania's privatisation law does not deal with large utilities, including Romtelecom, which form the economy's core and offer the best chances of luring big foreign investors.
The ministry has already worked out a draft for the transformation of utilities into shareholding companies, which it intends to submit to parliament for approval.

Romtelecom, which has some 2.8 million subscribers, is now undergoing an extensive upgrading programme, financed by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), in a bid to raise its market value ahead of privatisation.
A figure for Romtelecom's capital base was not available and Georgescu said Coopers & Lybrand were auditing the company.
"Privatising Romtelecom is the only way to rapidly align Romanian communications to European standards," Georgescu said.
Romania now has 13 telephone lines in 100 inhabitants.
"By the year 2002, Romtelecom will be a powerful unit, which will make it very difficult for other operators to penetrate the local market," Georgescu said.
